**Attunement.** You can attune to up to four magic items at once.

**Charges.** Whenever you use a magic item property that expends charges, roll 1d6. On a roll of 6, you use the property without expending the charges.

**Scrolls.** You can use any *Spell Scroll*, using Intelligence as your spellcasting ability for the spell. If the spell is a cantrip or a level 1 spell, you can cast it reliably. If the scroll contains a higher-level spell, you must first succeed on an Intelligence (Arcana) check (DC 10 plus the spell's level). On a successful check, you cast the spell from the scroll. On a failed check, the scroll disintegrates.

name: Spellcasting
description:
Drawing from your innate magic, you can cast spells. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Sorcerer spells, which appear in the Sorcerer spell list later in the class's description.

**Cantrips.** You know four Sorcerer cantrips of your choice. *Light*, *Prestidigitation*, *Shocking Grasp*, and *Sorcerous Burst* are recommended. Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Sorcerer cantrip of your choice.

When you reach Sorcerer levels 4 and 10, you learn another Sorcerer cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Sorcerer Features table.

**Spell Slots.** The Sorcerer Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

**Prepared Spells of Level 1+.** You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Sorcerer spells. *Burning Hands* and *Detect Magic* are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Sorcerer levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Sorcerer Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Sorcerer spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Sorcerer Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Sorcerer, your list of prepared spells can include six Sorcerer spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

If another Sorcerer feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Sorcerer spells for you.

**Changing Your Prepared Spells.** Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Sorcerer spell for which you have spell slots.

**Spellcasting Ability.** Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Sorcerer spells.

**Spellcasting Focus.** You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Sorcerer spells.

name: Innate Sorcery
description:
An event in your past left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with simmering magic. As a Bonus Action, you can unleash that magic for 1 minute, during which you gain the following benefits:

- The spell save DC of your Sorcerer spells increases by 1.
- You have Advantage on the attack rolls of Sorcerer spells you cast.

You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a Long Rest.

name: Font of Magic
description:
You can tap into the wellspring of magic within yourself. This wellspring is represented by Sorcery Points, which allow you to create a variety of magical effects.

You have 2 Sorcery Points, and you gain more as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Sorcery Points column of the Sorcerer Features table. You can't have more Sorcery Points than the number shown in the table for your level. You regain all expended Sorcery Points when you finish a Long Rest.

You can use your Sorcery Points to fuel the options below, along with other features, such as Metamagic, that use those points.

**Converting Spell Slots to Sorcery Points.** You can expend a spell slot to gain a number of Sorcery Points equal to the slot's level (no action required).

**Creating Spell Slots.** As a Bonus Action, you can transform unexpended Sorcery Points into one spell slot. The Creating Spell Slots table shows the cost of creating a spell slot of a given level, and it lists the minimum Sorcerer level you must be to create a slot. You can create a spell slot no higher than level 5.

Any spell slot you create with this feature vanishes when you finish a Long Rest.

Table: Creating Spell Slots

| Spell Slot Level | Sorcery Point Cost | Min. Sorcerer Level |
|------------------|--------------------|---------------------|
| 1                | 2                  | 2                   |
| 2                | 3                  | 3                   |
| 3                | 5                  | 5                   |
| 4                | 6                  | 7                   |
| 5                | 7                  | 9                   |

name: Metamagic
description:
Because your magic flows from within, you can alter your spells to suit your needs; you gain two Metamagic options of your choice from "Metamagic Options" later in this class's description. You use the chosen options to temporarily modify spells you cast. To use an option, you must spend the number of Sorcery Points that it costs.

You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it unless otherwise noted in one of those options.

Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your Metamagic options with one you don't know. You gain two more options at Sorcerer level 10 and two more at Sorcerer level 17.

name: Sorcerer Subclass
description: You gain a Sorcerer subclass of your choice. The Draconic Sorcery subclass is detailed after this class's description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Sorcerer levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Sorcerer level or lower.

name: Ability Score Improvement
description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see "Feats") or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Sorcerer levels 8, 12, and 16.

name: Sorcerous Restoration
description: When you finish a Short Rest, you can regain expended Sorcery Points, but no more than a number equal to half your Sorcerer level (round down). Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

name: Sorcery Incarnate
description:
If you have no uses of Innate Sorcery left, you can use it if you spend 2 Sorcery Points when you take the Bonus Action to activate it.

In addition, while your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you can use up to two of your Metamagic options on each spell you cast.

name: Epic Boon
description: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see "Feats") or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Dimensional Travel is recommended.

name: Arcane Apotheosis
description: While your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you can use one Metamagic option on each of your turns without spending Sorcery Points on it.

name: Draconic Resilience
description:
The magic in your body manifests physical traits of your draconic gift. Your Hit Point maximum increases by 3, and it increases by 1 whenever you gain another Sorcerer level.

Parts of you are also covered by dragon-like scales. While you aren't wearing armor, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Charisma modifiers.

name: Draconic Spells
description:
When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Draconic Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Table: Draconic Spells

| Sorcerer Level    | Spells                                                 |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| 3                 | Alter Self, Chromatic Orb, Command, Dragon's Breath    |
| 5                 | Fear, Fly                                              |
| 7                 | Arcane Eye, Charm Monster                              |
| 9                 | Legend Lore, Summon Dragon                             |

name: Elemental Affinity
description:
Your draconic magic has an affinity with a damage type associated with dragons. Choose one of those types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison.

You have Resistance to that damage type, and when you cast a spell that deals damage of that type, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell.

name: Dragon Wings
description:
As a Bonus Action, you can cause draconic wings to appear on your back. The wings last for 1 hour or until you dismiss them (no action required). For the duration, you have a Fly Speed of 60 feet.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest unless you spend 3 Sorcery Points (no action required) to restore your use of it.

name: Dragon Companion
description:
You can cast *Summon Dragon* without a Material component. You can also cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest.

Whenever you start casting the spell, you can modify it so that it doesn't require Concentration. If you do so, the spell's duration becomes 1 minute for that casting.

name: Eldritch Invocations
description:
You have unearthed Eldritch Invocations, pieces of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability or other lessons. You gain one invocation of your choice, such as Pact of the Tome. Invocations are described in the "Eldritch Invocation Options" section later in this class's description.

**Prerequisites.** If an invocation has a prerequisite, you must meet it to learn that invocation. For example, if an invocation requires you to be a level 5+ Warlock, you can select the invocation once you reach Warlock level 5.

**Replacing and Gaining Invocations.** Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your invocations with another one for which you qualify. You can't replace an invocation if it's a prerequisite for another invocation that you have.

When you gain certain Warlock levels, you gain more invocations of your choice, as shown in the Invocations column of the Warlock Features table.

You can't pick the same invocation more than once unless its description says otherwise.

name: Pact Magic
description:
Through occult ceremony, you have formed a pact with a mysterious entity to gain magical powers. The entity is a voice in the shadows—its identity unclear—but its boon to you is concrete: the ability to cast spells. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Warlock spells, which appear in the Warlock spell list later in the class's description.

**Cantrips.** You know two Warlock cantrips of your choice. *Eldritch Blast* and *Prestidigitation* are recommended. Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Warlock cantrip of your choice.

When you reach Warlock levels 4 and 10, you learn another Warlock cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Warlock Features table.

**Spell Slots.** The Warlock Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Warlock spells of levels 1–5. The table also shows the level of those slots, all of which are the same level. You regain all expended Pact Magic spell slots when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

For example, when you're a level 5 Warlock, you have two level 3 spell slots. To cast the level 1 spell *Charm Person*, you must spend one of those slots, and you cast it as a level 3 spell.

**Prepared Spells of Level 1+.** You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Warlock spells. *Charm Person* and *Hex* are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Warlock levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Warlock Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Warlock spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level no higher than what's shown in the table's Slot Level column for your level. When you reach level 6, for example, you learn a new Warlock spell, which can be of levels 1–3.

If another Warlock feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Warlock spells for you.

**Changing Your Prepared Spells.** Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Warlock spell of an eligible level.

**Spellcasting Ability.** Charisma is the spellcasting ability for your Warlock spells.

**Spellcasting Focus.** You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Warlock spells.

name: Magical Cunning
description: You can perform an esoteric rite for 1 minute. At the end of it, you regain expended Pact Magic spell slots but no more than a number equal to half your maximum (round up). Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

name: Warlock Subclass
description: You gain a Warlock subclass of your choice. The Fiend Patron subclass is detailed after this class's description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Warlock levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Warlock level or lower.

name: Ability Score Improvement
description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see "Feats") or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Warlock levels 8, 12, and 16.

name: Contact Patron
description:
In the past, you usually contacted your patron through intermediaries. Now you can communicate directly; you always have the *Contact Other Plane* spell prepared. With this feature, you can cast the spell without expending a spell slot to contact your patron, and you automatically succeed on the spell's saving throw.

Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a Long Rest.

name: Mystic Arcanum
description:
Your patron grants you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one level 6 Warlock spell as this arcanum.

You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a Long Rest before you can cast it in this way again.

As shown in the Warlock Features table, you gain another Warlock spell of your choice that can be cast in this way when you reach Warlock levels 13 (level 7 spell), 15 (level 8 spell), and 17 (level 9 spell). You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a Long Rest.

Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your arcanum spells with another Warlock spell of the same level.

name: Epic Boon
description: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see "Feats") or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.

name: Eldritch Master
description: When you use your Magical Cunning feature, you regain all your expended Pact Magic spell slots.

name: Dark One's Blessing
description: When you reduce an enemy to 0 Hit Points, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Charisma modifier plus your Warlock level (minimum of 1 Temporary Hit Point). You also gain this benefit if someone else reduces an enemy within 10 feet of you to 0 Hit Points.

name: Fiend Spells
description:
The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Fiend Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Table: Fiend Spells

| Warlock Level | Spells                                            |
|---------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| 3             | Burning Hands, Command, Scorching Ray, Suggestion |
| 5             | Fireball, Stinking Cloud                          |
| 7             | Fire Shield, Wall of Fire                         |
| 9             | Geas, Insect Plague                               |

name: Dark One's Own Luck
description:
You can call on your fiendish patron to alter fate in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add 1d10 to your roll. You can do so after seeing the roll but before any of the roll's effects occur.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), but you can use it no more than once per roll. You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

name: Fiendish Resilience
description: Choose one damage type, other than Force, whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest. You have Resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature.

name: Hurl Through Hell
description:
Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can try to instantly transport the target through the Lower Planes. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC, or the target disappears and hurtles through a nightmare landscape. The target takes 8d10 Psychic damage if it isn't a Fiend, and it has the Incapacitated condition until the end of your next turn, when it returns to the space it previously occupied or the nearest unoccupied space.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest unless you expend a Pact Magic spell slot (no action required) to restore your use of it.

name: Spellcasting
description:
As a student of arcane magic, you have learned to cast spells. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Wizard spells, which appear in the Wizard spell list later in the class's description.

**Cantrips.** You know three Wizard cantrips of your choice. *Light*, *Mage Hand*, and *Ray of Frost* are recommended. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Wizard cantrip of your choice.

When you reach Wizard levels 4 and 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Wizard Features table.

**Spellbook.** Your wizardly apprenticeship culminated in the creation of a unique book: your spellbook. It is a Tiny object that weighs 3 pounds, contains 100 pages, and can be read only by you or someone casting *Identify*. You determine the book's appearance and materials, such as a gilt-edged tome or a collection of vellum bound with twine.

The book contains the level 1+ spells you know. It starts with six level 1 Wizard spells of your choice. *Detect Magic*, *Feather Fall*, *Mage Armor*, *Magic Missile*, *Sleep*, and *Thunderwave* are recommended.

Whenever you gain a Wizard level after 1, add two Wizard spells of your choice to your spellbook. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown in the Wizard Features table. The spells are the culmination of arcane research you do regularly.

**Spell Slots.** The Wizard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

**Prepared Spells of Level 1+.** You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To do so, choose four spells from your spellbook. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Wizard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Wizard Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Wizard spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Wizard, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination, chosen from your spellbook.

If another Wizard feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Wizard spells for you.

**Changing Your Prepared Spells.** Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with spells from your spellbook.

**Spellcasting Ability.** Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

**Spellcasting Focus.** You can use an Arcane Focus or your spellbook as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.

name: Ritual Adept
description: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn't have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.

name: Arcane Recovery
description:
You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a Short Rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the slots can be level 6 or higher. For example, if you're a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels' worth of spell slots, regaining either one level 2 spell slot or two level 1 spell slots.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

name: Scholar
description: While studying magic, you also specialized in another field of study. Choose one of the following skills in which you have proficiency: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, or Religion. You have Expertise in the chosen skill.

name: Wizard Subclass
description:
You gain a Wizard subclass of your choice. The Evoker subclass is detailed after this class's description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Wizard levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Wizard level or lower.

> ### Expanding and Replacing a Spellbook
> 
> The spells you add to your spellbook as you gain levels reflect your ongoing magical research, but you might find other spells during your adventures that you can add to the book. You could discover a Wizard spell on a *Spell Scroll*, for example, and then copy it into your spellbook.
>
> **Copying a Spell into the Book.** When you find a level 1+ Wizard spell, you can copy it into your spellbook if it's of a level you can prepare and if you have time to copy it. For each level of the spell, the transcription takes 2 hours and costs 50 GP. Afterward you can prepare the spell like the other spells in your spellbook.
> 
> **Copying the Book.** You can copy a spell from your spellbook into another book. This is like copying a new spell into your spellbook but faster, since you already know how to cast the spell. You need spend only 1 hour and 10 GP for each level of the copied spell.
>
> If you lose your spellbook, you can use the same procedure to transcribe the Wizard spells that you have prepared into a new spellbook. Filling out the remainder of the new book requires you to find new spells to do so. For this reason, many wizards keep a backup spellbook.

name: Ability Score Improvement
description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see "Feats") or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Wizard levels 8, 12, and 16.

name: Memorize Spell
description: Whenever you finish a Short Rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of the level 1+ Wizard spells you have prepared for your Spellcasting feature with another level 1+ spell from the book.

name: Spell Mastery
description:
You have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a level 1 and a level 2 spell in your spellbook that have a casting time of an action. You always have those spells prepared, and you can cast them at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of those spells with an eligible spell of the same level from the book.

name: Epic Boon
description: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see "Feats") or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Spell Recall is recommended.

name: Signature Spells
description: Choose two level 3 spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, and you can cast each of them once at level 3 without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't cast them in this way again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot.

name: Evocation Savant
description:
Choose two Wizard spells from the Evocation school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Evocation school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

name: Potent Cantrip
description: Your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When you cast a cantrip at a creature and you miss with the attack roll or the target succeeds on a saving throw against the cantrip, the target takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

name: Sculpt Spells
description: You can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocations. When you cast an Evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 plus the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

name: Empowered Evocation
description: Whenever you cast a Wizard spell from the Evocation school, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of that spell.

name: Overchannel
description:
You can increase the power of your spells. When you cast a Wizard spell with a spell slot of levels 1–5 that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell on the turn you cast it.

The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a Long Rest, you take 2d12 Necrotic damage for each level of the spell slot immediately after you cast it. This damage ignores Resistance and Immunity.

Each time you use this feature again before finishing a Long Rest, the Necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12.

name: Iron Brace
description: When a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can take a Reaction to brace against it and reduce the damage by 1d8 + your Constitution modifier (minimum 1). You can do this a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

name: Stand Between
description: While your Rage is active, when a creature within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack you can see, you can take a Reaction to step into the blow: you take the damage instead, and you have Resistance to it.

name: Rallying Roar
description: As a Bonus Action you let out a roar that steadies your friends: you and each ally within 30 feet who can hear you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Barbarian level. You can do this once per Long Rest, or again by spending one use of your Rage.

name: Last Wall Standing
description: While your Rage is active, creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you have Disadvantage on attack rolls against any target other than you.

name: Kindled Blows
description: Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike, the blow deals an extra 1d6 Fire damage. The extra damage becomes 2d6 when you reach Barbarian level 10.

name: Heat-Forged
description: You have Resistance to Fire damage, and extreme heat does you no harm. While your Rage is active, flammable objects you strike that nobody is wearing or carrying catch fire.

name: Flashpoint
description: When you start a Rage, a wave of heat rolls off you: creatures of your choice within 10 feet make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + your Constitution modifier + your Proficiency Bonus), taking 2d8 Fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

name: Smouldering Retort
description: While your Rage is active, a creature within 5 feet of you that hits you with an attack takes Fire damage equal to your Constitution modifier plus your Rage Damage bonus.

name: Bedrock
description: Your Hit Point maximum increases by 1 for each Barbarian level you have, and the saving throw DC of your Grapple and Shove rises by 2.

name: Rooted
description: While your Rage is active, nothing can push you, pull you or knock you Prone against your will.

name: Rockslide Charge
description: If you move at least 20 feet in a straight line toward a creature and then hit it with a melee attack, it makes a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your Strength modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) or is pushed 10 feet away and knocked Prone.

name: Granite Skin
description: While your Rage is active, the first damage you take on each turn is reduced by your Constitution modifier plus your Rage Damage bonus.

name: Battle Cadence
description: You gain proficiency with Martial weapons. Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with a weapon, the blow rings with your song and deals an extra 1d6 Thunder damage.

name: Second Measure
description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. You can replace one of those attacks with a Bard cantrip that takes an action to cast (the Dungeon Master plays this swap).

name: Crescendo
description: When you cast a Bard spell with your action, you can make one weapon attack as a Bonus Action.

name: Rattling Jest
description: As a Bonus Action you aim a cruel jest at a creature you can see within 60 feet. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or has Disadvantage on its next attack roll. You can do this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once), and you regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

name: Practised Liar
description: You gain proficiency in the Deception and Insight skills.

name: A Second Face
description: You can cast Disguise Self without a spell slot a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining the uses on a Long Rest. You have Advantage on Deception checks to pass as someone you have studied for at least an hour.

name: The Last Mask
description: Once per Long Rest, when a creature attacks you, you can take a Reaction to slip behind a borrowed face: the attack misses, and the attacker is Frightened of you until the end of its next turn.

name: Hearthsong
description: As a Bonus Action you hum an old walking song and gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 1d8 + your Bard level. You can do this a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

name: Road-Wise
description: You gain proficiency in the Survival skill.

name: Well-Travelled
description: You and your companions cannot become lost except by magic, and companions who share a Short Rest with you regain extra Hit Points equal to your Charisma modifier.

name: Song of Homecoming
description: Once per Long Rest you can sing for one minute: each ally who hears the whole song regains Hit Points equal to your Bard level and ends one Charmed or Frightened condition on itself.

name: Hearth Domain Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Cleric level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Burning Hands, Heroism, Heat Metal and Flaming Sphere; level 5, Daylight and Protection from Energy; level 7, Fire Shield and Stone Shape; level 9, Flame Strike and Creation.

name: Banked Fire
description: When a Cleric spell you cast deals Fire or Radiant damage, it deals extra damage equal to your Wisdom modifier, once per casting.

name: Hearthkeeper's Welcome
description: As a Magic action you can spend a use of your Channel Divinity to kindle a welcoming warmth: you and each ally within 30 feet gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Cleric level.

name: Warmth Shared
description: Allies who finish a Short Rest with you regain extra Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier.

name: Hearth Never Cold
description: You have Resistance to Fire damage, and Fire damage from your spells ignores Resistance. Once per Long Rest, when you drop to 0 Hit Points, you drop to 1 instead, and creatures of your choice within 10 feet make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 4d8 Fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

name: Vigil Domain Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Cleric level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Shield of Faith, Command, Spiritual Weapon and Warding Bond; level 5, Spirit Guardians and Magic Circle; level 7, Guardian of Faith and Freedom of Movement; level 9, Hallow and Hold Monster.

name: Steadfast Guard
description: While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Class.

name: Sentinel's Rebuke
description: When a creature attacks an ally within 5 feet of you, you can take a Reaction and spend a use of your Channel Divinity to give that attack roll Disadvantage.

name: Interpose
description: When a creature within 5 feet of you is targeted by an attack, you can take a Reaction to trade places with it and become the attack's target instead.

name: Bastion
description: As a Magic action you can spend a use of your Channel Divinity to raise a holy bastion for 1 minute: you and allies within 10 feet gain a +2 bonus to Armor Class and cannot be Frightened.

name: Threshold Domain Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Cleric level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, False Life, Bane, Gentle Repose and Ray of Enfeeblement; level 5, Speak with Dead and Revivify; level 7, Death Ward and Blight; level 9, Raise Dead and Antilife Shell.

name: Ferryman's Due
description: When a fight you took part in ends in victory, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Cleric level + your Wisdom modifier.

name: Hand at the Gate
description: You can cast Spare the Dying as a Bonus Action, and its range is 60 feet for you.

name: Turn Back the Tide
description: When you heal a creature that has 0 Hit Points with a spell, it regains extra Hit Points equal to your Cleric level.

name: Close the Door
description: Undead have Disadvantage on saving throws against your spells. Once per Long Rest you can cast Revivify without a spell slot and without material components.

name: Thornwall Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Druid level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Entangle, Ensnaring Strike, Barkskin and Spike Growth; level 5, Plant Growth and Wind Wall; level 7, Stoneskin and Conjure Woodland Beings; level 9, Wall of Stone and Tree Stride.

name: Briar Mantle
description: As a Bonus Action you wrap yourself in living thorn and gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Druid level. You can do this twice, three times from Druid level 6 and four times from level 17, and you regain all uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

name: Hedge of Thorns
description: While you have Temporary Hit Points from Briar Mantle, a creature that hits you with a melee attack takes 1d6 Piercing damage.

name: Rooted Ground
description: Creatures you choose can move through the area of your Entangle and Spike Growth unhindered and unharmed.

name: Heartwood Guardian
description: Once per Long Rest, as a Magic action, you take on a heartwood hide for 1 minute: you have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing and Slashing damage, and allies within 10 feet of you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class.

name: Fallow Field Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Druid level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Ray of Sickness, False Life, Blindness/Deafness and Gentle Repose; level 5, Stinking Cloud and Plant Growth; level 7, Blight and Giant Insect; level 9, Contagion and Insect Plague.

name: Rot and Root
description: When a Druid spell of level 1 or higher that you cast deals Poison or Necrotic damage, it deals extra damage equal to your Wisdom modifier, once per casting.

name: Green from Grey
description: When one of your spells deals Poison or Necrotic damage, an ally within 30 feet of you regains Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).

name: Spore-Hardened
description: You have Resistance to Poison and Necrotic damage, and you cannot be Poisoned.

name: Fallow Season
description: Once per Long Rest you can call a fallow season into a 20-foot radius around you for 1 minute. Creatures of your choice that start their turn there make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 2d8 Necrotic damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

name: Hollow Hill Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Druid level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Sleep, Faerie Fire, Invisibility and Pass without Trace; level 5, Plant Growth and Meld into Stone; level 7, Hallucinatory Terrain and Dimension Door; level 9, Dream and Tree Stride.

name: Host's Gift
description: When you cast a spell with a spell slot that restores Hit Points, the creature regains extra Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier.

name: Under-Hill Paths
description: Once per Short or Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you can step into earth or a plant you touch and step out of another within 30 feet.

name: Glamoured Welcome
description: You cannot be Charmed, and fey creatures start out at least indifferent toward you unless you have wronged them.

name: The Hall Beneath
description: Once per Long Rest you can lead yourself and up to six allies into a hidden hall under the hill, where you take a Short Rest while only one minute passes outside.

name: Captain's Call
description: Companions fighting beside you add your Proficiency Bonus to their attack rolls.

name: Rallying Word
description: When you use Second Wind, one ally within 30 feet of you gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Fighter level.

name: Read the Field
description: You add your Intelligence modifier to your Initiative rolls, and you cannot be Surprised while you are not Incapacitated.

name: Strike on My Word
description: When you take the Attack action, you can give up one of its attacks so that an ally or companion who can see or hear you makes one weapon attack with its Reaction.

name: Hold the Ranks
description: Allies within 10 feet of you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class while you are not Incapacitated.

name: Last Command
description: Once per Long Rest, when an ally within 60 feet of you drops to 0 Hit Points, you can shout an order: it drops to 1 Hit Point instead and can make one attack with its Reaction.

name: Spark of the Art
description: You learn the Shocking Grasp and Fire Bolt cantrips. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for them.

name: Crackling Guard
description: When a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can take a Reaction to throw up a crackling ward and reduce the damage by 1d8 + your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1). You can do this a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

name: Spell and Steel
description: When you cast a cantrip with your action, you can make one weapon attack as a Bonus Action.

name: Unsettling Strike
description: A creature you hit with a weapon has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes against a spell you cast before the end of your next turn.

name: Fold the Distance
description: As a Bonus Action you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You can do this a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining the uses on a Long Rest.

name: Spellbreaker's Will
description: You have Advantage on saving throws against spells, and when you succeed on one you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Fighter level.

name: Plate and Grit
description: Your Hit Point maximum increases by 1 for each Fighter level you have.

name: Shield Bash
description: While you hold a Shield, you can replace one attack of your Attack action with a Shove made with the Shield.

name: Shoulder Into Them
description: When you Shove a creature, you can both push it 5 feet away and knock it Prone.

name: Shrug It Off
description: When you succeed on a Constitution saving throw, you regain Hit Points equal to your Constitution modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.

name: Unmoved
description: While you wear Medium or Heavy armor, damage you take from weapon attacks is reduced by 3.

name: Iron Will
description: Once per Long Rest, when you drop to 0 Hit Points and are not killed outright, you drop to a number of Hit Points equal to your Fighter level instead.

name: Crane's Poise
description: While you wear no armor and hold no Shield, you gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Class.

name: Wingbeat
description: When you use Step of the Wind, you can carry one willing ally within 5 feet of you along with you.

name: Settle the Storm
description: When an ally within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack, you can take a Reaction to turn the blow aside and reduce its damage by one roll of your Martial Arts die + your Wisdom modifier.

name: Still as Water
description: As a Bonus Action you can spend 1 Focus Point to grow perfectly still: attack rolls against you have Disadvantage until the start of your next turn.

name: Crane Ascending
description: When a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can take a Reaction to make one Unarmed Strike against it; on a hit it is also knocked Prone.

name: Serpent's Fang
description: Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature that is already wounded with an Unarmed Strike or a Monk weapon, the blow deals an extra 1d4 Poison damage. The extra damage becomes 2d4 when you reach Monk level 11. Your Martial Arts bonus strike can carry it too.

name: Shed Skin
description: You have Resistance to Poison damage, and as a Bonus Action you can spend 1 Focus Point to end the Poisoned condition on yourself.

name: Tightening Coil
description: A creature that fails its saving throw against your Stunning Strike also takes 2d6 Poison damage.

name: Patience of the Serpent
description: When you roll Initiative, choose a creature you can see: your first hit on it before the end of your next turn is a Critical Hit.

name: Slip Behind
description: Once on each of your turns, after you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike or a Monk weapon, your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn has Advantage.

name: Quiet Feet
description: You have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and as a Bonus Action you can spend 2 Focus Points to become Invisible until the end of your next turn or until you attack.

name: Fold of the Moment
description: Once per Short or Long Rest, when you take damage, you can take a Reaction to halve it and reappear in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet.

name: The Unseen Hand
description: Once per Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you become Invisible for 1 minute. Attacking does not end it, but you regain no Focus Points while it lasts.

name: Open Road Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Paladin level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Sanctuary and Longstrider; level 5, Warding Bond and Find Steed; level 9, Create Food and Water and Water Walk; level 13, Freedom of Movement and Locate Creature; level 17, Tree Stride and Commune with Nature.

name: Watchful Wayfarer
description: You add your Wisdom modifier to your Initiative rolls, and you gain proficiency in the Survival skill.

name: Shelter the Wayfarer
description: As a Bonus Action you can spend a use of your Channel Divinity to shelter an ally within 30 feet: for 1 minute it gains a +2 bonus to Armor Class while it stays within 30 feet of you.

name: Aura of the Road
description: You and allies within 10 feet of you ignore difficult terrain made of rubble, mud, snow or undergrowth, and have Advantage on saving throws against being knocked Prone.

name: Brigand's Bane
description: When a creature within 30 feet of you hits an ally, you can take a Reaction to move up to your Speed toward it without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Your next melee hit on it before the end of your next turn deals an extra 2d8 Radiant damage.

name: Lantern of the Long Road
description: Once per Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you raise a lantern of holy light for 10 minutes: allies within 30 feet regain 10 Hit Points at the start of their turns while above 0, and you and they have Advantage on Wisdom saving throws.

name: Ashes Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Paladin level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Searing Smite and Hellish Rebuke; level 5, Heat Metal and Misty Step; level 9, Fireball and Fear; level 13, Fire Shield and Locate Creature; level 17, Flame Strike and Geas.

name: Cinder Oath
description: Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon, the blow deals an extra 1d6 Fire damage.

name: Mark for Burning
description: As a Bonus Action you can spend a use of your Channel Divinity to name a creature within 60 feet. For 1 minute your first hit on it each turn deals extra Fire damage equal to your Charisma modifier, and you know which way it lies while it is within 1 mile.

name: Aura of Embers
description: Hostile creatures within 10 feet of you lose any Resistance to Fire damage.

name: Unquenched
description: Once per Long Rest, when you drop to 0 Hit Points and are not killed outright, you drop to 1 Hit Point instead.

name: Pyre-Bearer
description: Once per Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you become a walking pyre for 1 minute: your weapon hits deal an extra 2d8 Fire damage, melee attackers that hit you take 2d8 Fire damage, and you shed bright light for 30 feet.

name: Living Wood Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Paladin level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Goodberry and Entangle; level 5, Barkskin and Lesser Restoration; level 9, Plant Growth and Water Walk; level 13, Giant Insect and Freedom of Movement; level 17, Tree Stride and Wall of Stone.

name: Heartwood
description: Your Hit Point maximum increases by 1 for each Paladin level you have.

name: Bough and Root
description: As a Magic action you can spend a use of your Channel Divinity to call up roots: creatures of your choice within 15 feet make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or are Restrained until the end of your next turn.

name: Aura of Green Shelter
description: You and allies within 10 feet of you have Resistance to Poison damage and Advantage on saving throws against being Poisoned.

name: Deep Roots
description: While you stand on earth or living wood, nothing can move you or knock you Prone against your will. While you have half your Hit Points or fewer (but more than 0), you regain 5 Hit Points at the start of each of your turns.

name: Elder of the Grove
description: Once per Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you take on the shape of an elder of the grove for 1 minute: you have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing and Slashing damage, your reach grows by 5 feet, and allies within 30 feet regain 5 Hit Points at the start of their turns.

name: Trailbreaker Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Ranger level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Longstrider; level 5, Pass without Trace; level 9, Water Walk; level 13, Freedom of Movement; level 17, Tree Stride.

name: Trailbreaker's Lead
description: You have Advantage on Initiative rolls, and you gain proficiency in the Survival skill.

name: Sure-Footed
description: Difficult terrain does not slow you or the companions travelling with you, and you have Advantage on saving throws against being knocked Prone.

name: Ambush Lines
description: In the first round of a fight, your first weapon hit on a creature that has not yet acted deals an extra 2d8 damage of the weapon's type.

name: Vanish into the Land
description: You can take the Hide action as a Bonus Action while you are Lightly Obscured by foliage, mist or rubble.

name: Barrow Warden Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Ranger level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Protection from Evil and Good; level 5, See Invisibility; level 9, Speak with Dead; level 13, Death Ward; level 17, Dispel Evil and Good.

name: Hallowed Shot
description: Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with a weapon, the blow deals an extra 1d6 Radiant damage.

name: Tomb-Sense
description: You know when Undead are within 60 feet of you, though not exactly where, and you have Advantage on saving throws against being Frightened.

name: Lay to Rest
description: Undead you reduce to 0 Hit Points cannot rise again short of a Wish, and creatures of your choice within 10 feet of the fallen creature regain Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier.

name: Warden's Resolve
description: You have Resistance to Necrotic damage, and your Hit Point maximum cannot be reduced.

name: Packbound Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Ranger level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Animal Friendship; level 5, Animal Messenger; level 9, Conjure Animals; level 13, Dominate Beast; level 17, Commune with Nature.

name: Running with the Pack
description: Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature while a companion is fighting beside you, the blow deals an extra 1d6 damage of the weapon's type.

name: Shared Senses
description: Companions travelling with you add your Wisdom modifier to their Wisdom (Perception) checks.

name: Harrying Pack
description: When a companion beside you hits a creature, your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn has Advantage.

name: Pack Endures
description: Once per Short or Long Rest, when a companion within 30 feet of you drops to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction so that it drops to 1 Hit Point instead.

name: First Cut
description: In the first round of a fight, your first weapon hit on a creature deals an extra 1d6 damage of the weapon's type.

name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with the Disguise Kit and the Poisoner's Kit.

name: Borrowed Dark
description: You can take the Hide action as a Bonus Action while you are Lightly Obscured, and you have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks while you move at no more than half your Speed.

name: Quiet Hands
description: When you hit a creature that has not yet acted in the fight, it makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) or cannot speak or cry out until the end of its next turn.

name: The Last Cut
description: Once per Long Rest, when you hit a creature with a weapon, you can turn the hit into a Critical Hit.

name: Feint
description: As a Bonus Action you feint at a creature within 5 feet of you: your next attack roll against it before the end of your next turn has Advantage. You can do this a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

name: Smooth Talker
description: You gain proficiency in the Persuasion and Deception skills.

name: Read the Room
description: As a Bonus Action you study a creature you can see: you learn its attitude toward you and whether the next thing it says is a lie.

name: Silver Promise
description: Once per Long Rest, when you fail a Charisma (Persuasion) or Charisma (Deception) check, you can turn the failure into a success.

name: Unshakeable Story
description: You cannot be Charmed, and magic cannot read your thoughts or tell whether you are lying unless you allow it.

name: Trickwright Cantrips
description: You learn the Mage Hand, Minor Illusion and Shocking Grasp cantrips. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for them.

name: Unseen Fingers
description: Your Mage Hand is invisible, and you can use it to pick locks, lift purses or plant objects on someone, making the check yourself.

name: False Doubles
description: While a creature can see a double of you made with your Minor Illusion, its attack rolls against you have Disadvantage.

name: Spark Trap
description: As a Bonus Action you charge an object you touch. The next creature to touch it within 1 minute takes 3d8 Lightning damage, or half as much on a successful Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + your Intelligence modifier + your Proficiency Bonus).

name: Grand Misdirection
description: Once per Long Rest, when an attack or spell is aimed at you, you can take a Reaction to send it at another creature within 30 feet of you instead.

name: Frostblood Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Sorcerer level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Ice Knife, Fog Cloud, Gust of Wind and Hold Person; level 5, Sleet Storm and Protection from Energy; level 7, Ice Storm and Stoneskin; level 9, Cone of Cold and Wall of Stone.

name: Rime-Touched
description: When a Sorcerer spell of level 1 or higher that you cast deals Cold damage, it deals extra damage equal to your Charisma modifier, once per casting. Extreme cold does you no harm.

name: Hoarfrost Shell
description: When you are hit by an attack, you can take a Reaction and spend 1 Sorcery Point to gain Resistance to that attack's damage, and the attacker loses 10 feet of Speed until the end of its next turn.

name: Glacial Stride
description: You have Resistance to Cold damage, you ignore difficult terrain made of ice or snow, and you can walk across water by freezing it beneath your feet.

name: Heart of Winter
description: Once per Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you let winter loose for 1 minute: your Cold damage ignores Resistance, and creatures that start their turn within 10 feet of you take 2d8 Cold damage.

name: Veilborn Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Sorcerer level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Disguise Self, Silent Image, Invisibility and Darkness; level 5, Blink and Major Image; level 7, Greater Invisibility and Hallucinatory Terrain; level 9, Mislead and Seeming.

name: Step Behind the Veil
description: As a Bonus Action you fade half out of sight: the next attack roll a creature of your choice makes against you before your next turn has Disadvantage. You can do this a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

name: Through the Veil
description: When you cast an Illusion spell of level 1 or higher, you can teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

name: Half-There
description: You have Resistance to Psychic damage, and you can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain, taking 1d10 Force damage if you end a turn inside one.

name: Veilwalker
description: Once per Long Rest, as a Magic action, you step wholly behind the veil for 1 minute: you are Invisible, you see invisible things, and you can pass through objects. Attacking does not end it.

name: Saintblood Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Sorcerer level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Cure Wounds, Bless, Aid and Lesser Restoration; level 5, Revivify and Daylight; level 7, Death Ward and Guardian of Faith; level 9, Greater Restoration and Mass Cure Wounds.

name: Grace in the Blood
description: When you cast a spell with a spell slot that restores Hit Points, the creature regains extra Hit Points equal to your Charisma modifier.

name: Haloed
description: As a Bonus Action you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to wreathe yourself in a halo of bright light 20 feet across for 1 minute. Undead and Fiends in the light have Disadvantage on attack rolls against you.

name: Martyr's Grace
description: When an ally within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can take a Reaction to take that damage instead, with Resistance to it.

name: Miracle
description: Once per Long Rest, as a Magic action, you restore 70 Hit Points shared as you choose among creatures within 30 feet of you, and end the Blinded, Deafened and Poisoned conditions on them.

name: Lantern-Keeper Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Warlock level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Healing Word, Faerie Fire, Continual Flame and See Invisibility; level 5, Daylight and Sending; level 7, Locate Creature and Guardian of Faith; level 9, Commune and Greater Restoration.

name: Kindly Light
description: As a Bonus Action you draw on your patron's lamp and regain Hit Points equal to 1d8 + your Warlock level. You can do this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once), and you regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

name: Lamp in the Dark
description: You and creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you can see normally in magical darkness out to 30 feet.

name: Guiding Flame
description: Once per Short or Long Rest, when an ally within 60 feet of you fails a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to let it roll the save again.

name: Bring Them Home
description: Once per Long Rest, as a Magic action, you lead yourself and up to five allies by lantern-light to a place on this plane where you have rested before; you arrive after one minute.

name: Elder Grove Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Warlock level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Entangle, Goodberry, Barkskin and Spike Growth; level 5, Plant Growth and Speak with Plants; level 7, Conjure Woodland Beings and Giant Insect; level 9, Tree Stride and Awaken.

name: Bark and Bramble
description: When a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can take a Reaction to harden into bark and reduce the damage by 1d8 + your Charisma modifier (minimum 1). You can do this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once), and you regain all uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

name: Thorned Bargain
description: A creature within 5 feet of you that hits you with an attack takes Piercing damage equal to your Charisma modifier.

name: Green Passage
description: Once per Short or Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you can step into a tree or large plant you touch and out of another within 60 feet.

name: Grove's Embrace
description: Once per Long Rest, as a Magic action, you call on the grove to seize a creature within 60 feet. It makes a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or is Restrained for 1 minute, taking 4d10 Bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns; it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns.

name: Whispering Void Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Warlock level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Silent Image, Command, Mind Spike and Blindness/Deafness; level 5, Fear and Tongues; level 7, Arcane Eye and Resilient Sphere; level 9, Scrying and Dream.

name: Echo of the Void
description: When a Warlock spell you cast deals Force or Psychic damage, it deals extra damage equal to your Charisma modifier (half of it, rounded down, with a cantrip), once per casting (once per Eldritch Blast, not once per beam).

name: Void-Sight
description: Once per Short or Long Rest you can open your eyes to the void for 1 minute: you see through magical darkness and recognise illusions within 30 feet for what they are.

name: Unravelling Gaze
description: When a creature within 30 feet of you succeeds on a saving throw against one of your spells, you can take a Reaction to deal it Psychic damage equal to your Charisma modifier + your Warlock level.

name: Hollow Mind
description: You have Resistance to Psychic damage, and creatures you can see cannot Charm or Frighten you.

name: Call of the Deep Silence
description: Once per Long Rest, as a Magic action, you open a creature within 60 feet to the silence. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC: on a failure it takes 8d10 Psychic damage and is Incapacitated until the end of its next turn; on a success it takes half as much damage.

name: Woven Ward
description: While you wear no armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Intelligence modifier. The weave also steadies you: your hit point maximum increases by 1 for each Wizard level you have.

name: Ward-Scribe
description: Copying a spell that protects or wards into your spellbook takes you half the usual time and gold.

name: Spread the Ward
description: When an ally within 30 feet of you is hit by an attack, you can take a Reaction and expend a spell slot to give it Temporary Hit Points equal to twice the slot's level + your Intelligence modifier against that hit.

name: Sealed Mind
description: You have Advantage on saving throws against spells that would charm you or read your mind.

name: Woven Fortress
description: Once per Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you weave a fortress of wards for 1 minute: you and allies within 10 feet have Resistance to damage from spells.

name: Marrow-Cold
description: When a Wizard spell you cast deals Necrotic damage, it deals extra damage equal to your Intelligence modifier, once per casting.

name: Bone Servant
description: Once per Long Rest you can raise a small skeletal servant for 1 hour. It follows simple commands, can carry and fetch, and cannot attack.

name: Death's Chill
description: You have Resistance to Necrotic damage, and your Hit Point maximum cannot be reduced.

name: Command the Restless
description: Undead you create gain extra Hit Points equal to your Wizard level, and your spells that cover an area can leave them unharmed.

name: Unmaking Touch
description: Once per Long Rest, as a Magic action, you touch a creature. It makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 10d10 Necrotic damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

name: Foreseen Step
description: You add your Intelligence modifier to your Initiative rolls, a glimpse of each blow before it falls gives you a +1 bonus to Armor Class, and you cannot be Surprised while you are not Incapacitated.

name: Thread Pull
description: As a Bonus Action you tug at the thread of the moment around a creature you can see: the next attack it makes before the start of your next turn has Disadvantage. You can do this twice (three times from Wizard level 5), and you regain all uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

name: Glimpse Ahead
description: Once per Short or Long Rest you can cast Augury or Detect Thoughts without a spell slot.

name: Cut the Thread
description: When an attack hits an ally within 60 feet of you, you can take a Reaction and expend a spell slot to make it miss instead.

name: Weaver's Sight
description: You have Truesight out to 30 feet, and you can use Thread Pull four times per Short or Long Rest.

name: Snarewright Spells
description: You always have these spells prepared once you reach the Artificer level shown, and they never count against the spells you prepare: level 3, Grease and Alarm; level 5, Web and Spike Growth; level 9, Glyph of Warding and Sleet Storm; level 13, Black Tentacles and Stone Shape; level 17, Wall of Stone and Hold Monster.

name: Tangle-Bolt
description: As an action you fire a weighted line at a creature within 60 feet. It makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC: on a failure it takes 2d6 Piercing damage and is knocked Prone; on a success it takes half as much damage. You can do this a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once), and you regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

name: Trap-Maker's Kit
description: You gain proficiency with Tinker's Tools, and during a Short Rest you can set a snare on a 10-foot square you choose.

name: Barbed Lines
description: Your Tangle-Bolt deals 3d6 Piercing damage.

name: Chain Reaction
description: When a snare or a Tangle-Bolt catches a creature, a second creature within 10 feet of it makes the same saving throw.

name: Master of Snares
description: Your Tangle-Bolt deals 5d6 Piercing damage, and creatures have Disadvantage on saving throws against your snares.

name: Field Tonic
description: As a Bonus Action you drink a tonic you mixed in the field and regain Hit Points equal to 1d8 + your Intelligence modifier. You can do this a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once), and you regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

name: Reagent Boost
description: When you cast a spell that restores Hit Points or deals Acid, Fire or Poison damage, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one roll of it.

name: Restoring Draughts
description: You can cast Lesser Restoration without a spell slot a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, regaining the uses on a Long Rest, and a healing draught you hand to an ally restores extra Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier.

name: Proof Against Poison
description: You have Resistance to Acid and Poison damage, and you cannot be Poisoned.

name: Plated Craft
description: While you wear armor, you gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Class: you have fitted and tuned every plate of it yourself.

name: Second Swing
description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

name: Tuned Plating
description: Your armor counts as a magic item for you, and once per Short or Long Rest, when you are hit, you can take a Reaction to gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Artificer level.

name: Masterwork Suit
description: Your armor grants you Advantage on saving throws against being Grappled, Restrained or knocked Prone, and your Speed increases by 10 feet while you wear it.

name: Field Engine
description: As an action you fire a small arcane engine you built at a creature within 60 feet. It makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 2d8 Force damage on a failure or half as much on a success. The damage grows to 3d8 at Artificer level 9 and 4d8 at level 15. You can do this a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once), regaining the uses on a Long Rest.

name: Steadied Barrel
description: When you cast an Artificer spell that deals damage, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one of its damage rolls.

name: Burst the Engine
description: As a Magic action you can make your field engine burst: each creature within 10 feet of the point you choose makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 3d8 Force damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

name: Entrenched Battery
description: While you stand still behind your field engine, you and allies within 10 feet of you have Half Cover.

name: Smith's Drill
description: You gain proficiency with Martial weapons.

name: Forged Companion
description: You build a small mechanical companion that follows your commands. It acts on your turn, can take the Help action or make one attack, and you repair it during a Short or Long Rest (the Dungeon Master plays it).

name: Drilled Strikes
description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

name: Spark Strike
description: Once on each of your turns, when you or your companion hits a creature, you can deal an extra 2d6 Force damage to it, or restore 2d6 Hit Points to a creature within 30 feet. You can do this a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier per Long Rest.

name: Reforged Companion
description: Your companion gains a +2 bonus to Armor Class, and when it is hit it deals 1d4 + your Intelligence modifier Force damage back to the attacker.
